title: Performance and cost experiments
outcome: Explain performance and cost experiments using the deciding step in this fictional service.
scenario: Measure time and cost. Two fixed configurations answer the same six questions and meet the same quality rubric.
given: A totals 18 seconds and 12 cost units. B totals 12 seconds and 18 units.

steps.label: Compute mean time
steps.detail: A averages 3 seconds; B averages 2 seconds per case.

steps.label: Compute mean cost
steps.detail: A averages 2 units; B averages 3 units per case.

steps.label: Compare trade-off
steps.detail: B saves one second but costs one extra unit per case.

explanation: A fair performance experiment holds the workload and measurement procedure fixed. Faster is not automatically preferable under a budget.

counterfactual.change: Require at most 2 cost units per case.
counterfactual.prediction: A meets the budget; B does not.
counterfactual.reason: The mandatory resource condition changes the decision.

student_task: Calculate per-case seconds and cost units for A and B. Which meets a budget of at most 2 cost units per case, and what speed trade-off does that choice make?
teacher_answer: A averages 3 seconds; B averages 2 seconds per case. A averages 2 units; B averages 3 units per case. B saves one second but costs one extra unit per case. Changed case: A meets the budget; B does not. The mandatory resource condition changes the decision.
project_evidence: For the Grounded Learning Service, retain an annotated trace and the changed-case result. Name the contract or evidence that makes the deciding step valid, so another team can review it.
limits: Means hide variation; disclose workload, repeated runs and slow-case results before generalising.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice, distinct from the reserved independent case. These stipulated records illustrate reasoning; no real service execution or learner outcome is claimed.
